summary.headline: Raymond Q4 FY26 consolidated EBITDA fell to INR85 crore (13.9% margin) from INR99 crore, while Engineering segments grew and a INR930 crore 5-year capex plan was announced.
summary.overview: Consolidated total income rose 2% YoY to INR613 crore in Q4 FY26, but EBITDA fell to INR85 crore with a 13.9% margin versus INR99 crore and 16.4% a year earlier, as non-operating income dropped after INR600 crore was transferred to Raymond Realty post-demerger. For FY26, total income grew 10% to INR2,312 crore while EBITDA was flat at INR335 crore, with margin down to 14.5% from 15.9%. Aerospace & Defense revenue grew 26% for the year to INR392 crore, and Precision Technology & Auto Components grew 10% to INR1,667 crore with EBITDA up 34%, helped by synergies and a INR13 crore one-time land-sale gain. Management announced a INR930 crore five-year capex programme, including INR500 crore for Aerospace and INR430 crore for Precision Technology, with a new Andhra Pradesh aerospace plant targeted to start commercial production in the second half of calendar 2027.

segments.name: Aerospace & Defense (JK Maini Global Aerospace)
segments.commentary: Q4 FY26 revenue INR119 crore (+11% YoY) and EBITDA INR30 crore at 25.5% margin. FY26 revenue INR392 crore (+26%), EBITDA INR88 crore (+25%), margin 22.3%. Management guides to 25% annual growth.

segments.name: Precision Technology & Auto Components (JK Maini Precision Technology)
segments.commentary: Q4 FY26 revenue INR442 crore (+5%) with EBITDA INR67 crore at 15.2% margin. FY26 EBITDA INR223 crore (+34%) includes a one-time INR13 crore land-sale gain in Q2 FY26; management says margins should hold.

segments.name: Raymond Corporate (holding)
segments.commentary: Reported a loss of about INR13 crore in the other segment in the quarter. Management says it is broadly neutral over a full year, with interest income from the corpus offsetting expenses.

guidance_outlook: Management expects Aerospace to keep growing about 25% a year; the first 25% comes from the existing plant and the next from Andhra, which is seen as INR150-200 crore of incremental revenue in the second year.

Andhra Pradesh greenfield aerospace plant to start commercial production in the second half of calendar 2027, roughly the last quarter of FY28; little revenue expected in FY28 and real growth in FY29.

Precision Tech and Auto growth and margins are expected to stay at historical rates; management said FY27 growth would match past growth and margins would hold, with raw material inflation passed through with a lag.
Capex of INR930 crore over 5 years (INR500 crore Aerospace, INR430 crore Precision Tech), roughly INR100 crore per business per year, to be funded by internal accruals and debt.
Management targets 250 new aerospace parts this year against an earlier 300-350 per year guide, and says it will not run out of space before the Andhra plant is ready.
capex_capacity: Total capex plan of INR930 crore over five years: INR500 crore for Aerospace and INR430 crore for Precision Technology & Auto Components.
Andhra Pradesh aerospace plant on about 45 acres of new land; commercial production targeted for second half of calendar 2027.
Machines ordered on 6-8 month lead times; several machines on order for delivery over the next 3-6 months. Company sources from at least 15 machine manufacturers globally.
Management says the Andhra plant has no legacy baggage and will be used to move up the value chain, including heat treatment, surface treatment and assembly.
Aerospace vane capacity: management says the current plant has enough capacity for doubled vane orders before the Andhra plant is used.
demand_pricing: Management says customers are adjusting to US tariffs; automotive tariffs are now 18%, while aerospace had no tariffs. Some delays and rescheduling were reported.

Aerospace order book is cited at about INR2,300-2,350 crore over 5 years, per analyst questions; management says orders convert as products are qualified and ramped, and the book is not a fixed ceiling.
Over 75% of aerospace products are for engine programmes; the company has more than 25 customers and says it is derisking customer concentration.
Hybrid demand in Europe is described as stronger than EV demand; governments have pushed EV dates out 4-5 years.
Aerospace raw materials (titanium, Inconel, aluminium, stainless) are 100% imported today due to approval requirements; localisation is at an early stage, with progress expected in 6-8 months.
A first build-to-spec order was won, described as a self-designed product; the company did not disclose its value.
R&D is 3-5% of cost and is expensed in the year incurred; development costs are typically built into quoted prices.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the Precision Auto EBITDA margin expansion, and is it sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited SAP implementation in August, group integration, consolidated buying, cost reduction and efficiencies, and said margins should remain at current levels, with raw material pass-through lagging. The INR13 crore land-sale gain was excluded.

qa_highlights.question: What is the timeline and capex phasing for the Andhra plant?
qa_highlights.answer: Commercial production in the second half or last quarter of FY28 (calendar 2027). Capex of about INR100 crore per business per year, so roughly INR200 crore a year across both.

qa_highlights.question: How much incremental aerospace revenue will Andhra add in FY29?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to give numbers but said the first 25% growth year is met by the existing plant and the next comes from Andhra, which it framed as INR150-200 crore.

qa_highlights.question: How will the capex be funded given the INR68 crore net cash versus about INR1,000 crore borrowings in consolidated accounts?
qa_highlights.answer: Cash includes liquid and some 2-3 year marketable investments. Management said the Engineering business is self-funding from cash flows, with the parent's liquidity as a backstop, and no parent capital infusion is planned for organic needs.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the aerospace business is LEAP engine exposure, and what is the customer concentration?
qa_highlights.answer: Management would not split the order book by programme, but said over 75% of products are for engines across OEMs and that it serves more than 25 customers.

qa_highlights.question: Why is depreciation high relative to EBITDA?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said about INR800 crore of intangibles from the merger drive much of the depreciation, which is non-cash and gives a tax benefit, so cash generation is adequate.

risks_watch: Consolidated EBITDA fell 15% YoY in Q4 and the decline is driven by lower non-operating income after the INR600 crore transfer to Raymond Realty; core margin trend needs monitoring.
Aerospace growth depends on execution and on the Andhra plant starting on time; customer approvals and audits for a new location carry timing risk.
Raw material inflation from Middle East disruptions and dependence on imported aerospace-grade titanium and aluminium may pressure margins before pass-through.
Machine lead times and supply constraints could affect the pace of capacity additions.
Trade and tariff effects on automotive exports and some order rescheduling; EV demand in Europe is slower than expected.
summary.management_tone: Confident on long-term aerospace growth and the Andhra plan, but evasive on specifics such as order-book splits by engine programme, Andhra revenue numbers and the fine print of other income. Management was candid that Q4 was affected by Gulf logistics disruptions and that near-term outlook depends on macro factors.
key_quotes: So, we have planned it in such a way that we will not run out of space till we grow.
Ours is a modular growth, which happens every month.
And the margin will continue going forward as well because these are permanent synergies and cost reduction program that we've put in place.

adds.what: Andhra Pradesh greenfield aerospace plant on ~45 acres (commercial production H2 CY27, ~last quarter FY28)
Precision Tech & Auto capacity within INR430 crore 5-year capex plan (no specific plant identified)

growth.why: Management targets ~25% annual Aerospace growth through FY28, backed by existing-plant spare capacity (can grow 25% next year), an INR2,300-2,350 crore 5-year order book, and the Andhra plant (INR150-200 crore incremental revenue in year two) starting H2 CY27; Precision Tech growth guided to historical rates, but no specific new capacity for it is dated.
